# Objective

Use a two-part lab to separate **information admissibility** from **actual pretrained-model inference**.

- **Part A** audits whether context values and future covariates were genuinely available at a simulated historical forecast origin.
- **Part B** runs real zero-shot inference with Amazon Chronos-2 on a deterministic synthetic monthly series and compares the result with a seasonal-naive baseline.

Part B is a **retrospective technology counterfactual**, not a historical real-time OOS claim. A current pretrained model is being applied to a toy historical cutoff.

# Part A — Information-boundary audit

```bash
python labs/python/qm025_tsfm_information_audit.py
```

Move the availability date of `future_realized_macro` to the forecast origin and rerun. Then explain whether that change is a legitimate information assumption or merely a way to make the audit pass.

# Part B — Actual Chronos-2 zero-shot inference

The actual inference script follows the official Chronos dataframe interface: `BaseChronosPipeline.from_pretrained(...)` followed by `predict_df(...)`. The default model ID is `amazon/chronos-2`.

Install the optional runtime:

```bash
pip install -r labs/python/requirements-chronos2.txt
```

Then run:

```bash
python labs/python/qm025_chronos2_zero_shot.py
```

The first run may download the pretrained checkpoint (roughly 0.5 GB) if it is not already cached. `--device auto` uses CUDA when available and otherwise CPU.

For a governed experiment, pin a model revision rather than silently following `main`:

```bash
python labs/python/qm025_chronos2_zero_shot.py --revision <HUGGING_FACE_COMMIT_SHA>
```

The script reports the model ID/revision request, Chronos package version, device, Chronos-2 RMSE/MAE, seasonal-naive RMSE/MAE, and a toy 10–90% interval coverage diagnostic when those quantiles are returned.

# Offline contract check

The project gate does **not** require network access or a 0.5 GB model download. It validates the inference-data contract with:

```bash
python labs/python/qm025_chronos2_zero_shot.py --check-only
```

This checks context/holdout separation and forecast timestamps without importing or loading Chronos.

# Interpretation boundary

One synthetic holdout cannot establish that Chronos-2 is superior to conventional models. The purpose is to experience the real pretrained inference interface while keeping the epistemic boundary explicit:

> actual current-model inference + historical toy inputs ≠ historical live track record.

For current API details, use the [official Chronos repository](https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting) and the [Amazon Chronos-2 model card](https://huggingface.co/amazon/chronos-2).
